As referenced in section 38-81 state minimum fire safety standards adopted, incorporated by reference; amendments. The International Fire Code (IFC) is incorporated by reference. IFC outlines fire protection systems and appliances public and private. City ordinance requires the following in addition to those requirements of the IFC.
(a) [Fire hydrant installation.] Fire hydrants installed in the city shall meet ANSI/AWWA C205 standards, ISO standards and have a minimum of one 4½-inch steamer, or pumper connection, and two 2½-inch connections. All fire hydrants installed in the city shall be approved by the fire official, and the City of Fort Oglethorpe utilities department head. Fire hydrants without a pumper connection shall not be permitted. All hydrants cut off valves shall be accessible and readily identified. Hydrant cut off valves shall be located within a 3-foot. radius of the fire hydrant it serves unless otherwise authorized by the fire official, or City of Fort Oglethorpe utilities department head.
(b) Water supply. Adequate water supply to meet a minimum needed fire flow (NFF) as defined by ISO shall be provided for all buildings constructed within the city. More capacity may be required under certain circumstances by the fire official. Water mains, appliances, and fire hydrants shall be installed to provide the NFF or available water whichever is greater. All fire flow tests shall be witnessed by the fire official, or representative, prior to final approval. At no time shall a water main in a predominately commercial area, or serving a commercial structure, be less than 8 inches diameter and must meet NFPA 24 standards as adopted and amended by 120.3.3. At no time shall a water main serving any other area be less than 6 inches in diameter. No dead end water mains shall be permitted. All water mains shall be part of a grid, or loop, system to provide for the use of more than one hydrant at a time.
(c) Locations of fire hydrants. Approved fire hydrants shall be located every 300 feet. Fire hydrants may be located every 500 feet in those areas determined by the fire official to be predominately residential, one and two family dwellings only. Maximum distance from the nearest hydrant to the most remote exterior point of any building shall be 300 foot. The maximum distance may be increased to 500 feet for those one and two family dwellings determined by the fire official to be located in a predominately residential area. The distance shall be measured on a roadway surface meeting the fire department access requirements outlined in the SFPC, with distance being added for turns and obstacles that may increase the way hose may be laid.
(d) Maintenance. In addition to those requirements in the IFC, all hydrants found to be defective shall be repaired to proper working order within 36 hours of notification. If the hydrant is not repaired within the time specified the City of Fort Oglethorpe will repair the hydrant and all costs will be charged to the owner of said hydrant. The owner of said hydrant will be responsible for the maintenance and repair of hydrants, and will be charged for the repairs if done by the City of Fort Oglethorpe when a defective fire hydrant is found, when a fire hydrant is found to be out of service, and when a hydrant is fixed. Any fire hydrant not located within a public right-of-way or within an easement which has been deeded to the city shall be deemed private and will be the responsibility of the owner of the property where the fire hydrant is located.
(e) Obstruction. It shall be unlawful for any person to obstruct or hinder the approach of the Fire Department to any fire hydrants. In order to assure access to fire hydrants, the following requirements must be met:
(1) A minimum of 36 inches of clearance is required around a fire plug; and
(2) No person or entity shall construct any fence or other structure which would encroach the 36-inch minimum clearance for fire hydrants as outlined in subsection (1) of this section and no fence shall be constructed between the fire hydrant and the roadway; and
(3) Fire Hydrants shall not be buried, caps shall be at least 12 inches from grade; and
(4) No person shall allow trees, bushes or other growth upon the person's property to interfere with the approach to any fire hydrant or to encroach the 36-inch minimum clearance; and
(5) A fire plug may not be painted except by an authorized agent or employee of the fire department of the City of Fort Oglethorpe; and
(6) Parking of motor vehicles within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited. Parking lot lines may be required as necessary.
(f) [Exceptions.] Exceptions to the above shall be other installations acceptable to and approved by the authority having jurisdiction.
(Ord. No. 97-81, § 4-2-9, 1-26-1998; Ord. No. 2000-53, § 2, 12-11-2000; Ord. No. 2003-1, § 1, 3-24-2003; Ord. No. 2011-12, § 1, 3-14-2011)
595:
It shall be unlawful for any person to give or cause to be given a false alarm with the intent to deceive, or to pull the slide of any station or signal box, except in the case of fire. All fire alarms shall be maintained so not to cause undue false alarms.
(Ord. No. 97-81, § 4-2-19, 1-26-1998; Ord. No. 2000-53, § 2, 12-11-2000; Ord. No. 2003-1, § 1, 3-24-2003)
596:
It shall be unlawful for any person to injure, destroy, or in any manner interfere with the electric fire alarm of the city, or with the batteries, boxes, stations, wires, or other apparatus or appurtenances thereof, or used in connection therewith.
(Ord. No. 97-81, § 4-2-20, 1-26-1998)
597:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to have and maintain within the city any vacant lot or premises whereon flammable weeds, grasses and debris are permitted to remain after being notified by the fire marshall or the fire department of the city that the same constitutes a fire hazard.
(b) After ten days written notice to the owner, the city may, by its own forces, eliminate such fire hazard by the removal of such grasses, weeds, or other debris thereon and thereupon access the cost thereof against the owner of the property.
(Ord. No. 97-81, § 4-2-21, 1-26-1998)
598:
Any person who violates any of the provisions of this chapter or fails to comply therewith, shall for each and every violation and non-compliance respectively, be guilty of a misdemeanor, as defined by the state. The imposition of one penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation to continue. Penalties cannot exceed $1,000.00 or imprisonment of more than one year, or both, with the amount of fine/imprisonment being within the discretion of the municipal court of the city based upon the severity or repetition of the infraction.
(Ord. No. 97-81, § 4-2-22, 1-26-1998)
599:
As provided by law, the municipal court of the city shall have the venue and jurisdiction of any citations issued under this chapter.
(Ord. No. 97-81, § 4-2-23, 1-26-1998)
600:
(a) The city fire department may render aid and assistance during disastrous incidents and other immediate response emergencies outside its jurisdiction.
(b) The city fire department may form a mutual aid resource pact, known as the Georgia Mutual Aid Group, with other jurisdictions, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 25-6-1 et seq., the Georgia Mutual Aid Group being a public corporation.
(c) The Georgia Mutual Aid Group shall be governed by O.C.G.A. § 25-6-1 et seq.
(d) The city fire department fire chief or his/her designee shall be authorized to act on behalf of the city fire department on all matters relating to the activities and functions of the mutual aid resource pact once it has been established.
(e) The city fire department may withdraw from the Georgia Mutual Aid Group by resolution and vote of the city council pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 25-6-1 et seq.
(f) The city fire department's liabilities, privileges, and immunities, including those of its firefighters and other person's acting on its behalf, shall be governed by O.C.G.A. § 25-6-1 et seq.
(Ord. No. 99-54, §§ 1—6, 11-8-1999)
603:
There are adopted for the purposes of the public safety and welfare those certain fire prevention codes recognized as the state minimum fire safety standards and known as the National Fire Protection Association (National Fire Code and National Electrical Code), the American Insurance Association (National Building Code), the successor to the National Board of Fire Underwriters, the American Standards Association, and the Standard Building Code Congress (Standard Building Code) and the rules, regulations and amendments promulgated by the state safety fire commissioner that prevent the destruction of life and property by fire, explosion and related hazards, except such portions as are hereafter deleted, modified or amended. These codes, including the modifications and amendments, are incorporated by reference, and made part of this section as if fully set forth in this section. Copies of the specifications, rules and regulations shall be kept on file and open for public inspection in the office of the building official.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-31, 4-24-1995)
604:
(a) Purposes and intent. It is the primary purpose of this article to provide for the reasonable protection of life and property from the hazards created by fire, smoke, explosion or panic created from a fear of fire or smoke. It is the intent of this article to accomplish its purpose:
(1) Through educational efforts and programs designed to change high-risk attitudes and behaviors that are the root causes of most fire-related problems;
(2) Through consultations and informational programs, develop in people an awareness of the provisions of this article and other applicable laws, and aid them to determine the options available to correct hazards or problems noted; and
(3) By providing through this article reasonable, realistic and practical safeguards against fire and its related hazards. This article is declared to be remedial and shall be construed to secure beneficial interests and purposes, which are public safety, health and general welfare, through safety to life and property from fire, explosion and other hazards incident to the use and occupance of buildings, structures or premises.
(b) Scope.
(1) Applicability. The provisions of this article shall apply to all new and existing buildings, structures, premises, facilities and applicable conditions within the city; however, existing situations or conditions not in strict compliance with this article may be permitted to continue unless they are deemed by the fire marshal to constitute a distinct hazard to life or to property from fire, smoke or explosion. The provisions of this article shall not apply to the interior of one- or two-family dwellings or to the premises upon which such dwellings are located or to the interior of any apartment dwelling unit, provided such dwellings or apartments are used strictly for residential purposes. This article shall apply to such dwelling units whenever an activity coming under this article is conducted in such units and which creates a hazard from fire, smoke or explosion to life or to property.
(2) Federal and state authority. The provisions of this article shall not be held to deprive any federal or state agency or any applicable governing body having jurisdiction of any power or authority which it had on the effective date of the adoption of this article or of any remedy then existing for the enforcement of its orders, nor shall it deprive any individual or corporation of its legal rights as provided by law.
(3) Appendices. The appendices included in the codes adopted in section 38-81 are not intended for enforcement unless specifically referenced in the text of such codes.
(4) Referenced standards. Standards referenced in the codes adopted in section 38-81 shall be considered an integral part of such codes without separate adoption. If specific portions of a standard are denoted by code text, only those portions of the standard shall be enforced. Permissive and advisory provisions in a standard shall not be construed as mandatory.
(5) Existing buildings and special historic buildings. The provisions of this article shall apply to existing buildings or structures in the city; however, the provisions of such codes shall be coordinated by the fire marshal. The provisions of this article shall apply to special buildings or structures identified by the state or by the city as historic buildings; however, the provisions of this article shall be coordinated by the fire marshal with the applicable provisions of applicable state laws or regulations.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-32, 4-24-1995)
605:
There is created the bureau of fire prevention and community emergency education within the city for the purpose of implementing the provisions of this article. The bureau shall be under the direction and general supervision of the fire marshal. The fire marshal is responsible to the fire chief for the implementation of the provisions of this article and for the direction and supervision of the bureau. The bureau shall strive to improve the safety of the lives and property from fire and associated hazards within the city through programs of safety education through consultations, and through the inspection of buildings, structures, facilities and premises as often as deemed appropriate by the fire marshal. As the fire chief and fire marshal deem appropriate, the bureau may develop and implement, in coordination and cooperation with other departments, agencies or organizations, a comprehensive program of community emergency education.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-33, 4-24-1995)
606:
The fire chief shall recommend the fire marshal to the city council, who shall have discretion in appointment of the fire marshal. The fire marshal shall possess the required qualifications to be deputized by the state fire marshal. The fire marshal shall serve at the discretion of the council.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-34, 4-24-1995)
607:
The fire chief may detail or assign members of the fire department to the bureau of fire prevention and community emergency education to assist the fire marshal. Such members shall be under the direction and supervision of the fire marshal during their detail or assignment to the bureau. The fire chief, upon request of the fire marshal with approval by the city council, may fill positions deemed necessary for carrying out the purposes and programs of the bureau, in accordance with the personnel policies and regulations of the city. The selection shall be open to members and nonmembers of the fire department. Personnel assigned to fill positions with the bureau shall be under the direction and supervision of the fire marshal.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-35, 4-24-1995)
608:
The chief of police, the city marshal, the building official or law enforcement officers of the city shall render assistance to the fire marshal or the fire chief in the implementation and enforcement of this article upon the request of the fire marshal, or as appropriate, the fire chief.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-36, 4-24-1995)
609:
The fire marshal is authorized to inspect, or to cause to be inspected, as he deems appropriate or necessary based on fire experience in the community, on complaint, or on other applicable grounds, and as resources permit, buildings, structures, premises and facilities coming within the scope of this article. The purpose of such inspections is to ascertain if any condition exists which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire or explosion or that could contribute to the spread of a fire or its by-products, or to ascertain any significant nonconformance with the purposes, intent and other provisions of this article or of any other applicable law, rule or regulation affecting safety to life and/or property from fire, explosion or related hazards. The fire marshal is authorized to apply other applicable laws, and to cause to be corrected any condition which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire or explosion, or that could contribute to the spread of a fire, or any significant nonconformance with the purposes, intent or provisions of this article affecting safety to life and/or property from fire, explosion or related hazards.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-37, 4-24-1995)
610:
The fire marshal or his authorized representatives may, to the extent permitted by law, have free access to and the right to enter at all reasonable times any building, structure, facility or premises coming under the scope of this article, whether completed or under construction, for the purpose of conducting inspections and otherwise implementing the provisions of this article. Before entering any building, structure, facility or premises not normally open to the public, except when a fire or other emergency condition exists or has occurred, the fire marshal or his representative shall obtain the consent of the occupant, owner or person in charge at the time. Where consent to enter is refused, the fire marshal may seek an order or an administrative search warrant from the municipal court, or if deemed appropriate, from the superior court of Catoosa County authorizing his entry or that of his representatives for the purpose of conducting the inspection or investigation. The term "emergency condition," for purposes of this section, shall mean any condition or circumstance which the fire marshal or fire chief judges to constitute an immediate threat or danger to the occupants of the building, structure, facility or premises or to persons or property exposed to a fire, the hazards associated with fire, explosion, the threat of fire or explosion, or exposed to risks from some other hazardous condition or circumstance.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-38, 4-24-1995)
611:
Any application for or the acceptance of any approval, permit, license or certificate requested, or required pursuant to this article or other applicable law or ordinance of this city or state, constitutes agreement and consent by the person making the application, or accepting the approval, permit, license or certificate to allow the fire marshal or his representatives to enter the building, structure, facility or premises at any reasonable time to conduct inspections as may be deemed appropriate by the fire marshal or as otherwise provided by this article or other applicable ordinances, rules, regulations or state law.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-39, 4-24-1995)
612:
(a) Whenever the fire marshal or his designated representative finds any violation of this article or any fire hazard, he is authorized to issue or serve a written notice of the findings of an inspection as set forth in this chapter and to notify the building official.
(b) Whenever the fire marshal or his designated representative finds any violation of this article or any fire hazard which is deemed to create a serious or significant potential threat to life in event of fire or explosion, he is authorized to issue a written order to correct or abate the violation or hazard. Such order when issued shall set forth a reasonable and realistic time frame or date limit for correction, abatement or compliance. The time frame for correction, abatement or compliance established by or as directed by the fire marshal, or his designated representative, may be reasonably correlated by him to the seriousness or relative degree of hazard, and/or to the complexity of the means of correction or abatement.
(c) Where deemed necessary, due to the potential of risk of life or property, the fire marshal may issue a verbal order for the immediate correction or abatement of a violation or fire hazard. This may be followed by a written order or notice of action.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-40, 4-24-1995)
613:
The fire marshal or the fire chief shall have the authority to summarily abate any violation of this article or any fire hazard which constitutes an immediate or imminent danger or threat to life in their opinion, and where the following of the provisions for obtaining corrective action or abatement as set forth elsewhere in this article is not practical in their judgment.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-41, 4-24-1995)
614:
An unsafe building or structure is any building or structure which is deemed to be structurally unsafe or which is not provided with adequate means of egress, or which is deemed to constitute a serious fire hazard, or which is otherwise deemed dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use constitutes a hazard to the safety, health or welfare of the public by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, obsolescence, fire damage, disaster damage, vandalism, flood damage or abandonment, as specified in this article or by any other applicable codes or ordinances in force in the city.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-42, 4-24-1995)
615:
(a) The service of notices or orders issued in connection with this section may be made by the fire marshal or his representative upon the owner, occupant or person in charge of the building, structure, facility, premises or portion thereof where the hazard or violation was found, or by delivering a copy of the notice or order to any or all of the persons noted. If such person cannot be served by delivery as noted, service may be accomplished by affixing a copy of the notice or order in a conspicuous place at or near the entrance of the building, structure, facility or premises, or by delivering or sending a copy of the notice or order to the known agent of the owner or occupant, or in the event of an absentee owner with no known agent, by sending a copy by certified or registered mail to the owner's last known residence, business or post office address.
(b) If the building, structure, facility or premises is owned by one or more persons and is occupied by one or more other persons under lease or otherwise, the notice or order issued in connection with this section shall apply to the addition to or changes in the building, structure or premises such as would immediately become real estate and become the property of the owner and not the occupant unless it is otherwise agreed between or among the owner and the occupant.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-43, 4-24-1995)
616:
(a) Any person who shall fail to comply with an order of correction or abatement as set forth in this section, or who shall build or act in violation of this article or of any detailed statement of specifications or plans submitted and approved under authority of this article in connection with any approval, certificate or permit issued under this article, or who shall perform any act deemed to create a serious potential for fire or explosion and for which the issuance of an order to correct or abate is not adequate, and who is found guilty shall be guilty of a violation of this article. A person found guilty under this section shall, for each and every violation and noncompliance respectively, be subject to punishment as provided in Charter section 4.13. The imposition of penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation or permit it to continue, and the responsible person shall be required to correct or abate such violation within a time limit as ordered by the court. When not otherwise specified, each five days a prohibited condition or violation continues following an order of the court to correct or abate such violation within a time limit as ordered by the court to correct or abate the condition shall constitute a separate offense.
(b) When the fire marshal, the fire chief or their authorized representative determine that violations of this article warrant the filing of charges or action of the court as provided for in subsection (a) of this section, the issuing of a citation of charges and/or summons to appear before the municipal court upon request of the fire marshal, the fire chief or their authorized representative, is authorized.
(c) In addition to the filing of charges as specified in subsections (a) and (b) of this section or as a separate remedy at law, the fire marshal or fire chief may seek injunctive relief for any fire hazard, violation or condition that threatens the safety of life based on the provisions of this article or any applicable code or ordinance of the city or of the state.
(d) The application of penalties by the court as provided for in subsection (a) of this section shall not be held to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or violations.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-44, 4-24-1995)
617:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to use a building, structure, facility or premises in violation of the provisions of this article where an order has been affixed to the building prohibiting the use of the building under authority of any provision of this article without the approval of the fire marshal or his authorized representative or the court.
(b) When it is determined that the occupancy or use of a building has changed from that shown on the certificate of occupancy issued by the building official, the fire marshal may issue such notice or orders as necessary and in conformance with this article to remove or remedy any noted violations or hazards and he shall refer the building to the building official for any repairs, alterations, remodeling, removing or demolition required.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-45, 4-24-1995)
618:
(a) The planning, design and construction of new buildings, structures, facilities or premises shall be in conformance with the building code, electrical code, gas code, mechanical code, zoning code and the life safety code, as adopted by the city council; however, where operations, contents, processes or conditions are not covered by such codes, the applicable provisions of this article shall apply.
(b) Any alterations, additions or changes required in existing buildings, structures, facilities or premises because of a change in use, occupancy, exit design or other reason shall be made in compliance with the codes noted in subsection (a) of this section and as set forth in section 38-81.
(c) The fire marshal and the building official shall coordinate their review of plans on new construction and/or renovations or alterations of existing buildings so as to ascertain compliance with the codes and standards under their respective jurisdictions.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-46, 4-24-1995)
619:
(a) New construction. The fire marshal and the building official shall have the authority to jointly consider and approve a modification of any of the applicable codes for new construction with regard to matters relating to fire protection and safety to life in event of fire or related emergencies where the proposed design fire protection system, building use, or construction method involved is unusual or where such involves an unusual hazard, condition or hardship, and the provisions of the codes and standards of force do not clearly or adequately deal with the proposed design, protection system application or design, building use, or construction method, in their judgment.
(b) Alternate materials. It is the intent of this section to allow the use of designs, systems, methods or devices of equivalent or superior quality, strength, fire resistance, effectiveness, durability and safety to those prescribed by the applicable codes and standards, provided technical documentation, data, or other information or material acceptable to the fire marshal and building official is submitted for review and such demonstrates to their satisfaction the equivalency of the design, system, method or device for the intended use. Any modification or alternate safeguard jointly approved by the fire marshal and building official shall not afford a condition less safe to life and, where appropriate, property, than in their judgment would be provided with compliance with the provisions of applicable codes.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-47, 4-24-1995)
620:
(a) Existing conditions. The fire marshal shall have the authority to grant a variance to the provisions of this article, or of the codes or standards adopted by reference by this article, upon application in writing by the owner and/or occupant of an existing building, structure, facility or premises, or by his authorized agent, when there are practical difficulties in the way of carrying out the strict letter of this article or the codes or standards adopted by reference by this article or the city. Such modification or variance may be granted by the fire marshal provided in his judgment the spirit, intent and purposes of this article are observed, the public safety shall be reasonably and practically secured, the modification is in the interest of the community, and substantial justice will be done. The particulars of any variance granted or allowed and the decision of the fire marshal shall be approved or disapproved by the city council at its next duly scheduled meeting.
(b) Right to appeal. Whenever the fire marshal or fire chief shall issue an order pursuant to this article, disapprove an application, refuse to grant a permit, refuse to grant a waiver or modification, or when it is claimed that the provisions of this article or the codes and standards adopted by reference by this article or the city do not apply or that their true intent and meaning have been misconstrued or wrongly interpreted, the applicant or aggrieved party may appeal from the order or decision of the fire marshal or fire chief to the board of adjustments and appeals as established by the adopted building code of the city within 30 days after the decision is rendered by the fire marshal or fire chief. The provisions of the applicable building code relative to time limits, variations and modifications, and decisions as connected with the appeals to the board, shall be applicable to appeals from the fire marshal or the fire chief relating to this article. If not satisfied with the decision of the board, appeal may be made to the court of appropriate jurisdiction. Every decision of the board relative to this article shall be filed in the office of the fire marshal.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-48, 4-24-1995)
621:
(a) Interference with fire officials. It shall be unlawful for any person to interfere with, abuse or obstruct in any way the fire chief, fire marshal or their representatives in carrying out any actions in accordance with their official duties as set forth by this article, or by any other applicable local ordinance, or by any law or regulation of the state.
(b) Unlawful use of credentials; unlawful impersonation of fire official. It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized person to use an official or unofficial badge or credential so as to impersonate an authorized fire official or to otherwise impersonate a fire official.
(c) Authority to investigate fires, explosions, false alarms or related incidents. The fire marshal or his authorized representatives are authorized to investigate the cause, origin and circumstances of any fire or explosion, or to investigate any incident resulting from the sending or sounding of a false alarm of fire or a bomb threat. When in the judgment of the fire marshal reasonable cause exists that a fire or explosion may have been of criminal origin, the fire marshal or his authorized representative is authorized to locate and take custody of any or all physical evidence relating to the cause of the fire or explosion and to continue the investigation to the extent deemed appropriate within the limits of fire prevention bureau resources and within the limits of applicable state laws. The fire marshal shall inform the police department of each fire of criminal or suspected criminal origin, false alarms or bomb threats. Also, he shall assist the police department in its investigations of reported incidents if so requested by that department. The police department shall be responsible for the investigation of fires and/or explosions of criminal or suspected criminal origin, false alarms or bomb threats so as to identify, apprehend and assist in the prosecution of the person responsible for such criminal act.
(d) Evacuation of buildings, structures, facilities or premises. When, in the judgment of the fire marshal, the fire chief or their authorized representatives in their absence, there is an actual or serious potential danger to the occupants of or persons in close proximity of any building, structure, facility or premises because of unsafe structural conditions, the presence of explosives, explosive fumes or vapor, toxic fumes, gases or materials, the fire marshal, the fire chief, or their authorized representatives in their absence, may order the complete or partial immediate evacuation of any building, structure, facility or premises and, as necessary, areas in such proximity to these as to be endangered. All persons under order to evacuate shall promptly leave the evacuation area and shall not reenter until authorized to do so by the official who issued the evacuation order. This section shall not pertain to bomb threats where no bomb or explosive device is known to exist. In such bomb threat situations, the decision to evacuate or not to evacuate is the responsibility of the person in charge of the building, structure, facility or premises at that time.
(e) Permits and approvals. No person shall maintain, store or handle materials, or conduct processes which produce conditions hazardous to life or property, or install equipment used in connection with such activities without first obtaining approval, or as appropriate based on the provisions of this article, a permit from the fire marshal. Where conditions or activities are also regulated by a state or federal agency and a permit, license or certificate is required by the regulating agency, no local permit is required; however, the approval of the fire marshal is required and he shall have the authority to apply the provisions of this article where a hazardous condition is discovered.
(f) Tests. All equipment required by this article or other applicable codes adopted by the city or by the state shall be maintained in a safe, sound and operational condition. The fire marshal may require tests or test reports as proof of compliance. Required tests are to be made at the expense of the owner or his agent by an approved testing laboratory or other approval agency or firm acceptable to the fire marshal.
(g) Authority to expose or stop work. Whenever any construction or installation coming under this article is subject to inspection prior to use and is covered or concealed without having first been inspected, the fire marshal may require by verbal and/or written order that such work be exposed for inspection. The fire marshal shall be notified when the installation is ready for inspection within a reasonable period of time. When any construction or installation work is being performed in violation of the plans, specifications or understandings as approved by the fire marshal, a written order may be issued to the responsible party to stop work on that portion of the work which is in violation. The order shall state the nature of the violation. No work shall be continued on that portion until the violation has been corrected.
(h) Administrative liability. Any officer or employee of the city empowered or authorized to administer or act under the provisions of this article or other applicable codes in force in the city or adopted or required by the state, and acting for the city or state in the discharge of his duties, shall not be held liable personally; and he is relieved from all personal liability from any damages that may accrue to any person or property as a result of any act required, implied or permitted, in the discharge of his duties, or as required, implied or permitted by this article or other applicable codes in force in the city or adopted or required by the state.
(i) Municipal liability. The city shall not be liable for any damage to persons or property resulting from any act or any failure to act in connection with any provision of this article or other applicable codes in force in the city or adopted or required by the state.
(j) Permitting and inspection. The inspection or permitting of any building or plan by any employee of the division of fire prevention of the fire department under the requirements of this article shall not be construed in any court as a warranty of the physical condition of such building or the adequacy of such plan. Neither the city or any employee of the city shall be liable in tort for damages for any defect or hazardous or illegal condition or inadequacy in such building or plan, nor for any failure or any component of such building, which may occur subsequent to such inspection or permitting.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-49, 4-24-1995)
622:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Approved means acceptable to the fire marshal, or as appropriate, the fire chief, of the city. In determining acceptability of installations, equipment, materials or procedures, the fire marshal, or as appropriate the fire chief, may base acceptance on compliance with nationally recognized standards. The fire marshal, or as appropriate the fire chief, may require evidence of proper installation, proper use or use of proper procedures. The fire marshal, or as appropriate the fire chief, may also refer to listings or labeling practices of recognized testing laboratories, inspection agencies or other recognized organizations concerned with product evaluations and which are in a position to determine compliance with appropriate standards for the current production of listed items and the satisfactory performance of such equipment or materials in actual usage.
Building code means the building code adopted in section 18-51.
Building official means the building official of the city.
Chief of police means the Chief of the Fort Oglethorpe Police Department, Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia.
Chief of the fire department or fire chief means the fire chief of the Fort Oglethorpe Fire Department, Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia.
Combustible means capable of undergoing combustion.
Electrical code means the electrical code adopted in section 18-51.
Exit discharge means that portion of a means of egress between the termination of an exit and a public way.
Fire hazard means:
(1) Any thing or act which increases or may cause an increase of the hazard or menace of fire to a greater degree than that customarily recognized as normal by persons in the public service regularly engaged in preventing, suppressing or extinguishing fire;
(2) Any thing or act which may obstruct, delay, hinder or interfere with the operations of the fire department or with the egress of occupants in event of fire;
(3) A condition which will increase the spread or extent of fire; or
(4) A definite condition of materials, rather than the materials themselves, which has the potential to produce a fire cause.
Gas code means the gas code adopted in section 18-51.
Mechanical code means the mechanical code adopted by section 18-51.
Overcrowding means a condition:
(1) When there are more people in the building or portion of the building than is allowed or posted in accordance with the building code, or where applicable, the state safety fire law; or
(2) When in the judgment of the fire marshal or his representative a threat to the safety of life exists due to the number of persons sitting or standing so as to obstruct or impede the use of aisles, passages, corridors, exits or other components of required means of egress.
Zoning code means the zoning code in appendix A of this Code.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-50, 4-24-1995)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
623:
(a) Permit required. No person shall maintain, store or handle materials or conduct processes which produce conditions hazardous to life or property, or install equipment used in connection with such activities without first obtaining approval, or as appropriate, a fire regulatory permit from the fire marshal as provided; however, the approval of the fire marshal is required, and he shall have the authority to apply the provisions of this article where a hazardous condition is discovered.
(b) New activities. Any person desiring to conduct or engage in any new process or activity requiring a fire regulatory permit under this article shall apply for a permit as set forth in this section and shall be issued the permit prior to engaging in the conducting of the process or activity, or before occupying a building or structure requiring a permit.
(c) Existing activities. Persons known to be conducting processes or activities required to be permitted under this article on or before the date of adoption of this article, shall be advised that a permit is required. Such persons may also be advised of any violations noted under this article that must be corrected before a permit can be issued. The fire marshal shall exercise reasonableness and shall apply the applicable provisions of sections 38-81 and 38-98 when applying the provisions of this article or of any of the technical standards adopted by reference under this article or otherwise adopted by the city council, when such are being applied to existing conditions or activities. No existing process or activity requiring a permit under this article and found to be in significant noncompliance with the applicable provisions of this article shall continue after a period of one year from the date the person is notified of the permit requirement. Where there is noncompliance, the fire marshal may issue a temporary permit with an established expiration date. A temporary permit issued in connection with this subsection may be extended provided a plan of corrective action has been submitted prior to the expiration of the permit, evidence clearly indicates that compliance is being obtained, and there are practical difficulties in completing the corrective action by the expiration date.
(d) Permitted action. A fire regulatory permit shall constitute permission to maintain, store or handle materials, or to conduct processes which may produce conditions hazardous to life or property, or to install equipment used in connection with such activities. A permit shall not be a substitute for any license or certificate required by law. A permit issued shall be construed to be a license to proceed with work and shall not be construed as authority to violate, cancel, alter or set aside any of the provisions of this article. The issuance of a permit shall not be construed as preventing the fire marshal from thereafter requiring correction of errors in plans or in construction, or of violations of this article.
(e) Transfer of permit prohibited. A fire regulatory permit shall not be transferable, and any change in use or occupancy of a building or premises shall require a new permit. A fire regulatory permit shall continue until revoked or for such a period of time as designated at the time of issuance.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-51, 4-24-1995)
624:
(a) Application for permit. An application for a permit shall be made to the fire marshal on a form available at the division of fire prevention. The form shall be fully completed. The application shall be accompanied by such data as may be required by the fire marshal and by the required fee, as set forth in subsection (c) of this section.
(b) Agreement to comply; responsibility. The filing of an application for a permit or a request for an approval from the fire marshal under this article constitutes an agreement on the part of the person the applicant represents to comply with the provisions of this article and of the technical codes and standards adopted by reference under this article or otherwise adopted by the city council. Such filing shall also constitute an understanding on the part of the permittee that the permittee, not the city, the fire marshal or the fire chief, shall bear the full responsibility for any damages to persons and/or property in connection with any fire, explosion or other accident or event involving any process, material, installation or activity covered by a permit or approval issued in connection with any of the provisions of this article.
(c) Processing fee. There shall be a processing fee as stated in the schedule of fees and charges for the issuance of a fire regulatory permit. The fee shall accompany the permit application when it is filed. If an inspection conducted to determine compliance with this article reveals that a condition exists which would preclude the issuance of a permit, the processing fee shall not be refunded. Further, where a permit is denied due to violations and hazards noted, the activity for which the permit is required shall not be deemed in compliance. The fire marshal may require the filing of a new application and fee if he deems the original application and fee to have been filed prematurely or filed with false or incomplete information. Such fee shall not be required of government, charitable or religious organizations.
(d) Review of applications; issuance. The fire marshal or his authorized representative shall review applications submitted and issue approvals or permits as required provided the data on the application and plans and specifications submitted with the application indicate to a reasonable degree compliance with the provisions of this article and the technical codes and standards adopted by reference under this article or otherwise adopted by the city council. Permits for activities requiring evidence of financial responsibility on the part of the permittee as required by this article shall not be issued unless proof of required financial responsibility is furnished.
(e) Rejected. If an application for a permit or approval is rejected by the fire marshal or his authorized representative, the applicant shall be advised of the reasons for such rejection.
(f) Display of permits. A copy of the fire regulatory permit shall be posted or shall otherwise be readily accessible at each place a permitted activity is performed. As required by the fire marshal, a permit holder may be required to carry the permit.
(g) Records. A record of fire regulatory permits issued and any exceptions granted shall be maintained in the fire prevention bureau. Such record shall be available for public inspection during normal business hours upon request to the fire marshal.
(h) Duration of permits; limitations on issuance. A fire regulatory permit issued under this article shall continue until revoked or for the period of time designated in the permit at the time of issuance of the permit. The permit shall be issued to one person only and for the location or purpose described in the permit. Any change which affects any of the conditions of the permit shall require a new permit. The fire marshal may grant an extension of the permit period where an expiration date has been established upon presentation by the permittee of a satisfactory reason for failure to start or complete the work or activity authorized by the permit by the designated expiration date. A permit issued shall become invalid unless the use authorized by such is commenced within six months after issuance, or if the use authorized by such permit is suspended or abandoned for a period of six months after the time the use of the permit is commenced. One or more extensions of time, for periods not to exceed 90 days each, may be allowed for the permit provided the extension is requested in writing and justifiable cause is demonstrated. Extensions granted by the fire marshal shall be in writing.
(i) Temporary permit. When a potentially hazardous situation or activity of a temporary nature is encountered, and is not specifically regulated by this article, a permit may be required by and issued by the fire marshal to cover the duration of the situation or activity. He shall require the filing of an application and fee as set forth for a regular fire regulatory permit.
(j) Consolidated permit. Only one permit shall be required for each location of a firm which may be required to obtain more than one permit under the permit requirements of this article. Such consolidated permit shall list all of the materials or activities covered by the permit. Revocation of any of the permitted materials or activities covered by the consolidated permit shall require the revocation of the permit and issuance of a new permit. In such situation, a new and revised permit may be issued by the fire marshal for the materials or activities not covered by the revocation. No new application is required and no fee is required for the revised consolidated permit.
(k) Revocation of permits. The fire marshal may revoke his approval of a permit issued under the provisions of this article when it is determined there has been any false statements or misrepresentation as to the material facts in the application or in the plans on which the approval or permit was based. Further, the fire marshal may revoke his approval or a permit upon determination by him that the occupancy, operation or activity for which the approval or permit or was issued is in violation of or is not in conformity with the provisions of this article or with other applicable codes adopted by the city or with applicable laws, rules or regulations of the state jurisdiction; and the fire marshal may notify the responsible agency of any noted violation, nonconformance or condition deemed to be hazardous.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § 4-2-52, 4-24-1995)
626:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
(a) A fire permit is issued by the fire department of the City of Fort Oglethorpe allowing for the outdoor burning of a limited nature during the burning period. (b) A fire control device is an operable fire extinguisher or operating water hose attached to a functioning and open water hydrant.
(c) A blue permit when issued by the fire office of the City of Fort Oglethorpe allows for the reduction of leaves on the premises on which they fall by the person in control of the premises, or for disposal of tree limbs from storm damage as outlined in the Rules for Air Quality Control, chapter 391-3-1 (5)(a), (1) and (7).
(d) A white permit is required for burning on construction sites, in heavily populated areas, or other areas not outlined in the blue print. A white permit shall be issued without an inspection of the proposed burning area and material first being conducted by an authorized agent of the fire department of the City of Fort Oglethorpe, and payment of the inspection and issuance fee determined by the fire department of the City of Fort Oglethorpe.

(f) Structure or dwelling is any man made building, whether for commercial, public or personal use, or other improvement upon real property.

(i) Waste disposal service is the city garbage collection and disposal service or any public or private entity performing garbage collection and disposal within the incorporated limits of the City of Fort Oglethorpe.

628:

To insure as far as possible, the safety of the citizens and personnel of the city from the possible harmful effects of hazardous materials, the following article is adopted as an amendment to the fire prevention and protection ordinance to insure that the quantities and types of hazardous chemicals and extremely hazardous substances will be known and regulated within the city to insure as far as possible the safety of the citizens of the city from the dangers of hazardous materials.
(Ord. No. 97-81, § 4-5-1, 1-26-1998)
634:
The following article is applicable to any facility that is required to prepare or have available material safety-data sheet(s) (MSDS) for hazardous chemicals under the Federal Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970 and all regulations promulgated under that act, and any facility required to submit reports for extremely hazardous substances, as defined in 40 C.F.R. 355, Appendix A, and any facility owning, handling, transporting, storing or in any other manner or method dealing in class A, B and C explosives and blasting agents within the city.
(Ord. No. 97-81, § 4-5-2, 1-26-1998)
635:
(a) The owner or operator of a facility subject to this article shall submit a material safety data sheet and any other required forms to the fire safety division, of the fire department.
(b) Forms must be submitted on all hazardous chemicals present at the facility at any one time in amounts equal to or greater than 9,000 pounds (or 3,540 kilograms) and for all extremely hazardous substances present at the facility in an amount greater than or equal to 500 pounds (or 227 kilograms which is approximately 55 gallons) or the threshold planning quantity (TPQ), whichever is lower as defined in Title 40, Part 355, Appendix A of the Code of federal regulations, which provision is incorporated herein.
(1) The owner or operator of a facility that is subject to this part shall submit the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Tier 24 to the fire and safety division, of the fire department, on an annual basis beginning on September 1, 1998.
(2) The owner and operator will also be required to submit a material safety data sheet on all hazardous chemicals as designated by Title 29 Code of Federal Regulations section 1910.120, which provisions are incorporated herein.
(3) The term hazardous chemical does not apply to the following:
a. Any food, food additive, color additive, or cosmetic regulated by the Food and Drug Administration.
b. Any substance present as a solid in any manufactured item to the extent exposure to the substance does not occur under normal conditions of use.
c. Any substance to the extent it is used for personal, family, or household purposes, or is present in the same form and concentration as a private package for distribution and used by the general public.
d. Any substance to the extent it is used in a research laboratory or a hospital, or other medical facility under the direct supervision of a technically qualified individual.
(c) The facility will be subject to unannounced inspections by the fire safety division of the fire department to insure compliance with the requirements of this chapter.

636:
(a) All locations within the city limits that contain hazardous materials must label all containers in conformity with current DOT guidelines.

644:
Enforcement officers shall refer to any duly authorized law enforcement officer employed by the city.
Fine lanes are areas designated by the fire official providing access for fire department vehicles to buildings, fire department connections and fire hydrants. This includes all alleys, driveways or lanes, devoted to public use, where the parking of motor vehicles or other obstructions can interfere with ingress or egress of fire department vehicles for the protection of person and properties including, but not limited to, shopping centers, theaters, hospitals, bowling lanes, churches, multi-family housing, and high-rise buildings.

Master plans means all original plans drawn in accordance with this chapter; all copies distributed shall be from this original drawing.
Need fire flow as defined by insurance services office fire suppression rating schedule.
New building for the purpose of this chapter shall mean any commercial or public facility whose plans were submitted after this amendment goes into effect.
Plats shall refer to maps created by the building owner and approved by the fire marshal or his designee which depict the location and boundaries of land and all existing fire lanes in accordance with this chapter. Such maps shall be drawn to scale.
Property owners shall refer to each person, firm, corporation, or entity possessing any estate, or leasehold right in the property being designated as fire lanes.
Ticket shall mean an order issued out of court by an enforcement officer of the city directing a violator of this chapter to comply with all civil fine set forth.

(a) Every existing building shall be accessible to fire department apparatus by way of access roadways with all-weather driving surfaces of not less than 20 feet (6.1 m) of unobstructed clear width, with adequate roadway turning radius capable to supporting the imposed loads of the fire apparatus and having a minimum vertical clearance of 13 feet 6 inches (4.1 m).
(1) Where fire protection systems approved by the fire official are provided, the above required clearances may be modified by the fire official.
(2) The fire official shall have the authority to require an increase in the minimum access widths where they are inadequate for fire or rescue operations.

There shall be a minimum roadway turning radius of 35 feet (10.6 m). Three shall be a minimum vertical clearance of 13 feet 6 inches (4.1 m). The designated fire lanes shall be paved, purred concrete, or equivalent, capable of supporting the gross vehicle weight of fire apparatus.
(1) Where fire protection systems approved by the fire official are provided, the above required clearances may be modified by the fire official.

(Ord. No. 2001-17, § 1, 8-27-2001)
648:

(a) Enforcement of this section shall be through a civil action municipal court by the issuance of a ticket which shall be either left with the vehicle or delivered to the person in possession thereof. (1) The first violation of parking in a fire lane within any 30 day period shall be punished by a $50.00 civil fine; provided, however the second violation within any 30 day period shall be punishable by a civil fine of $80.00; and a civil fine of $100.00 may be levied for each violation thereafter occurring within any 30 day period.

In the event the civil fine is not paid within 48 hours, the municipal court may issue a warrant for failure to appear requiring the offender to show cause why he failed to pay the fine within 48 hours, the municipal court may issue a citation for contempt requiring the offender to show cause why he failed to pay the fine within the time frame allowed by this section. 649:

(Ord. No. 2001-17, § 1, 8-27-2001)

658:
(a) The flood hazard areas of the city are subject to periodic inundation which results in loss of life and property, health and safety hazards, disruption of commerce and governmental services, extraordinary public expenditures for flood and relief and protection, and impairment of the tax base, all of which adversely affect the public health, safety and general welfare.

661:
Unless specifically defined below, words or phrases used in this chapter shall be interpreted so as to give them the meaning they have in common usage and to give this chapter its most reasonable application.
Accessory structure means a structure having minimal value and used for parking, storage and other non-habitable uses, such as garages, carports, storage shed, pole barns, hay sheds and the like.
Addition (to an existing building) means any walled and roofed expansion to the perimeter of a building which the addition is connected by a common load-bearing wall other that a firewall. Any walled and roofed addition, which is connected by a firewall or is separated by an independent perimeter load-bearing wall, shall be considered "new construction."
Appeal means a request for a review of the city building official's interpretation of any provision of this chapter.
Area of shallow flooding means a designated AO or AH zone on a community's flood insurance rate map (FIRM) with base flood depths from one to three feet, and/or where a clearly defined channel does not exist, where the path of flooding is unpredictable and indeterminate, and where velocity flow may be evident.
Area of special flood hazard is the land in the floodplain within a community subject to a one percent or greater chance of flooding in any given year. In the absence of official designation by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, areas of special flood hazard shall be those designated by the local community and referenced in section 42-7.
Base flood means the flood having a one percent chance of being equaled or exceeded in any given year.
Basement means that portion of a building having its floor subgrade (below ground level) on all sides.
Building means any structure built for support, shelter, or enclosure for any occupancy or storage.
Critical facility means any public or private facility, which, if flooded, would create an added dimension to the disaster or would increase the hazard to life and health. Critical facilities include:
(1) Structures or facilities that produce, use, or store highly volatile, flammable, explosive, toxic, or water-reactive materials;
(2) Hospitals and nursing homes, and housing for the elderly, which are likely to contain occupants who may not be sufficiently mobile to avoid the loss of life or injury during flood and storm events;
(3) Emergency operation centers or data storage centers which contain records or services that may become lost or inoperative during flood and storm events; and
(4) Generating plants, and other principal points of utility lines.
Development means any man-made change to improved or unimproved real estate, including, but not limited to, buildings or other structures, mining, dredging, filling, grading, paving, excavating, drilling operations, and permanent storage or materials or equipment.
Elevated building means a non-basement building built to have the lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area elevated above the ground level by means of fill, solid foundation perimeter walls, pilings, columns, piers, or shear walls adequately anchored so as not to impair the structural integrity of the building during a base flood event.
Existing construction is any structure for which the "start of construction" commenced before April 27, 1988 (i.e. the effective date of the first floodplain management code or ordinance adopted by the community as a basis for that community's participation in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)).
Existing manufactured home park or subdivision means a manufactured home park or subdivision for which the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including at a minimum the installation of utilities, the construction of streets, and final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads) is completed before April 27, 1988 (i.e. the effective date of the first floodplain management regulations adopted by a community).
Expansion to an existing manufactured home park or subdivision means the preparation of additional sites by the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the manufactured homes are to be affixed, including the installation of utilities, the construction of streets, and either final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads.
Flood or flooding means a general temporary condition of partial or complete inundation of normally dry land areas from:
(1) The overflow of inland or tidal waters; or
(2) The unusual and rapid accumulation runoff of surface waters from any source.
Flood hazard boundary map (FHBM) means an official map of a community, issued by the federal insurance administration, where the boundaries of areas of special flood hazard have been defined as zone A.
Flood insurance rate map (FIRM) means an official map of a community, issued by the federal insurance administration, delineating the areas of special flood hazard and/or risk premium zones applicable to the community.
Flood insurance study the official report by the federal insurance administration evaluating flood hazards and containing flood profiles and water surface elevations of the base flood.
Floodplain means any land area susceptible to flooding.
Floodproofing means any combination of structural and non-structural additions, changes, or adjustments to structures, which reduce or eliminate flood damage to real estate or improved real property, water and sanitary facilities, structures and their contents.
Floodway means the channel of a river or other watercourse and the adjacent land areas that must be reserved in order to discharge the base flood without cumulatively increasing the water surface elevation more than a designated height.
Freeboard means a factor of safety usually expressed in feet above a flood level for purposes of floodplain management. "Freeboard" tends to compensate for the many unknown factors that could contribute to flood heights greater than the height calculated for a selected size flood and floodway conditions, such as wave action, bridge openings, and the hydrological effect of urbanization of the watershed.
Highest adjacent grade means the highest natural elevation of the ground surface, prior to construction, adjacent to the proposed foundation of a building.
Historic structure means any structure that is:
(1) Listed individually in the National Register of Historic Places (a listing maintained by the U.S. Department of Interior) or preliminarily determined by the secretary of the interior as meeting the requirements for individual listing on the National Register;
(2) Certified or preliminarily determined by the secretary of the interior as contributing to the historical significance of a registered historic district or a district preliminarily determined by the secretary to qualify as a registered historic district;
(3) Individually listed on a state inventory of historic places and determined as eligible by states with historic preservation programs which have been approved by the secretary of the interior; or

a. By an approved state program as determined by the secretary of the interior, or
b. Directly by the secretary of the interior in states without approved programs.
Lowest floor means the lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area, including basement. Manufactured home means a building, transportable in one or more sections, built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities. The term also includes park trailers, travel trailers, and similar transportable structures placed on a site for 180 consecutive days or longer and intended to be improved property.
Mean sea level means the average height of the sea for all stages of the tide. It is used as a reference for establishing various elevations within the floodplain. For purposes of this chapter, the term is synonymous with National Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD).
National Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD) as corrected in 1929 is a vertical control used as a reference for establishing varying elevations within the floodplain.
New construction means any structure for which the "start of construction" commenced on or after April 27, 1988 and includes any subsequent improvements to the structure (i.e., the effective date of the first floodplain management ordinance adopted by the community as a basis for community participation in the (NFIP)).
New manufactured home park or subdivision means a manufactured home park or subdivision for which the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including at a minimum, the installation of utilities, the construction of streets, and either final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads) is completed on or after April 27, 1988 (i.e., the effective date of the first floodplain management regulations adopted by a community).
North American Vertical Datum (NAVD) as corrected in 1988 is a vertical control used as a reference for establishing varying elevations within the floodplain.
Recreational vehicle means a vehicle, which is:
(1) Built on a single chassis;
(2) 400 square feet or less when measured at the largest horizontal projection;
(3) Designed to be self-propelled or permanently tow able by a light duty truck; and
(4) Designed primarily not for use as a permanent dwelling but as temporary living quarters for recreational, camping, travel, or seasonal use.
Start of construction means the date the development permit was issued, provided the actual start of construction repair, reconstruction, or improvement was within 180 days of the permit date. The actual start means the first placement of permanent construction of the structure such as the pouring of slabs or footings, installation of piles, construction columns, or any work beyond the stage of excavation, and includes the placement of a manufactured home on a foundation. Permanent construction does not include initial land preparation, such as clearing, grading and filling; nor does it include the installation of streets and/or walkways; nor does it include excavation for a basement, footings, piers or foundations or the erection of temporary forms; nor does it include the installation on the property of buildings appurtenant to the permitted structure, such as garages or sheds not occupied as dwellings units or part of the main structure (note: accessory structures are not exempt from any chapter requirements). For a substantial improvement, the actual start of construction means the first alteration of any wall, ceiling, floor or other structural part of a building, whether or not that alteration affects the external dimensions of the building.
Structure means a walled and roofed building that is principally above ground, a manufactured home, a gas or liquid storage tank.
Substantial damage means damage of any origin sustained by a structure whereby the cost of restoring the structure to its before damaged condition would equal or exceed 50 percent of the market value of the structure before the damage occurred.
Substantial improvement means any reconstruction, rehabilitation, addition or other improvement of a structure, taking place during a five-year period, in which the cumulative cost equals or exceeds 50 percent of the market value of the structure prior to the "start of construction" of the improvement.
The market value of the structure should be:
(1) The appraised value of the structure prior to the start of the initial repair or improvement; or
(2) In the case of damage, the value of the structure prior to the damage occurring.
The term includes structures, which have incurred "substantial damage" regardless of the actual amount of repair work performed. For the purposes of this definition, "substantial improvement" is considered to occur when the first alteration of any wall, ceiling, floor or other structural part of the building commences, whether or not that alteration affects the external dimensions of the building. The term does not, however, include:
(1) Those improvements of a structure required to comply with existing violations of state or local health, sanitary or safety code specification which are solely necessary to assure safe living conditions and which have been identified by the code enforcement official, and not solely triggered by an improvement or repair project; or
(2) Any alteration of a "historic structure" provided that the alteration will not preclude the structure's continued designation as a "historic structure."
Substantially improved existing manufactured home parks or subdivisions is where the repair, reconstruction, rehabilitation or improvement of the street, utilities and pads equals or exceed 50 percent of the value of the streets, utilities and pads before the repair, reconstruction or improvement commenced.
Variance is a grant of relief from the requirements of this chapter which permits construction in a manner otherwise prohibited by this chapter.
Violation means the failure of a structure or other development to be fully compliant with the community's floodplain management regulations. In all areas of special flood hazard the following provisions are required:
(1) New construction and substantial improvements of existing structures shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement of the structure.
(2) New construction and substantial improvements of existing structures shall be constructed with materials and utility equipment resistant to flood damage.
(3) New construction and substantial improvements of existing structures shall be constructed by methods and practices that minimize flood damage.
(4) Elevated buildings. All new construction or substantial improvements of existing structures that include any fully enclosed area located below the lowest floor formed by foundation and other exterior walls shall be designed so as to be an unfinished or flood resistant enclosure. The enclosure shall be designed to equalize hydrostatic flood forces on exterior walls by allowing for the automatic entry and exit of floodwater.
a. Designs for complying with this requirement must either be certified by a professional engineer or architect or meet the following minimum criteria:
1. Provide a minimum of two openings having a total net area of not less than one square inch for every square foot of enclosed area subject to flooding;
2. The bottom of all openings shall be no higher than one foot above grade; and
3. Openings may be equipped with screens, louvers, valves or other coverings or devices provided they permit the automatic flow of floodwater in both direction.
b. So as not to violate the "lowest floor" criteria of this chapter, the unfinished or flood resistant enclosure shall only be used for parking of vehicles, limited storage of maintenance equipment used in connection with the premises, or entry to the elevated area; and
c. The interior portion of such enclosed area shall not be partitioned or finished into separate rooms.
(5) All heating and air conditioning equipment and components (including ductwork), all electrical, ventilation, plumbing, and other service facilities shall be designed and/or located so as to prevent water from entering or accumulating within the components during conditions of flooding.
(6) Manufactured homes shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse, or lateral movement. Methods of anchoring may include, but are not limited to, us of over-the-top or frame ties to ground anchors. This standard shall be in addition to and consistent with applicable state requirements for resisting wind forces.
(7) New and replacement water supply systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of flood waters into the system.
(8) New and replacement sanitary sewage systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of flood waters into the systems and discharges from the systems into flood waters.
(9) On-site waste disposal systems shall be located and constructed to avoid impairment to them or contamination from them during flooding.

Where base flood elevation data are available, new construction and/or substantial improvement of any structure or manufactured home shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated no lower than one foot above the base flood elevation. Should solid foundation perimeter walls be used to elevate a structure, openings sufficient to facilitate equalization standards of section 42-61(4), "Elevated buildings."

A registered professional engineer or architect shall certify that the design and methods of construction are in accordance with accepted standards of practice for meeting the provisions above, and shall provide such certification to the official as set forth above and in section 42-43(6).
(3) Standards for manufactured homes and recreational vehicles. Where base flood elevation data are available:
a. All manufactured homes placed and/or substantially improved on:
1. Individual lots or parcels;
2. In new and/or substantially improved manufactured home parks or subdivisions;
3. In expansions to existing manufactured home parks or subdivisions; or
4. On a site in an existing manufactured home park or subdivision where a manufactured home has incurred "substantial damage" as the result of a flood,
Must have the lowest floor including basement, elevated no lower than one foot above the base flood elevation.
